parsed.explanation: No visitor-facing restriction is documented: trans presentation is not criminalised (sodomy struck down Dec 2022, itself brought by a trans claimant), borders/foreign documents draw no friction, and no facility, custody or care rule targets trans people. But recourse is weak where it was tested: the sole documented anti-trans attack (meat cleaver, 2018) ended in a $460 fine with no jail — in a small island jurisdiction one case carries real statistical weight, and the state response was itself damning, signalling impunity rather than rule-of-law protection. Official rhetoric (anti-refugee statements, ministers framing LGBT claims as foreign imposition, fundamentalist churches urging discrimination) coexists with a pro-LGBT PM, court remediation and growing Pride visibility — a split, not uniformly hostile, climate. Employment exclusion of trans people is a resident-facing gap, not a visitor exposure. Weak remedies plus dated violence plus thin unresolved records (custody, healthcare, regional case) hold this in elevated-to-reduced territory: more protected than hostility-without-recourse profiles, clearly below jurisdictions demonstrating working enforcement.
